title: Dynamic memory margining and KV failover policy for batch surge resilience
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Goal: reduce OOMs and tail latency spikes during sudden batch surges by introducing a dynamic memory margin ("margining") and a deterministic KV failover policy that gracefully demotes cached KV segments when headroom is constrained. This flows across weights/KV/activations budgeting and ties into continuous batching scheduling decisions.
background: We observe intermittent OOMs and sharp eviction storms when multiple high-token requests arrive concurrently and the batching window packs more sequences than anticipated. Current static watermarks and ad-hoc eviction policies either (a) leave too much unused reserved headroom hurting utilization or (b) react too late causing eviction cascades and increased tail latency. Existing tickets explored predictive headroom and reserve ledgers, but runbooks are still reactive.
proposal: Introduce an adaptive soft-margin computed per-GPU that (1) scales with observed batch queue depth, token length quantiles, and recent peak KV residency; (2) is expressed as an elastic token-equivalent budget (surge absorber). Implement a KV failover policy that: prefer-demotes non-critical KV entries (recently unused, low-entropy layers) into a GPU-eviction tier with metadata retained on host memory or compressed on-GPU; fall back to full eviction only when margin budget is exhausted. Tie margin size to a probabilistic peak predictor (EWMA + 95th percentile multiplier) for conservative but not wasteful headroom. Expose controls to pin margins per-tenant and an autoscaling hint to Dedicated pools.
implementation_plan: Design: finalize margin heuristic and token-to-bytes conversion (2d)
Simulation: build micro-simulator that replays production traces to validate margin sizing under mixed workloads (3d)
Runtime: implement margin bookkeeping in memory ledger and eviction hooks (4d)
KV failover: add demotion path that moves candidates to compressed host cache or compact GPU slab (5d)
Scheduler integration: surface margin utilization to batcher and allow adaptive batching thresholds (2d)
Canary rollout: 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 2 weeks with telemetry dashboards
acceptance_criteria: Simulator shows >= 3x reduction in OOM rate on replayed surge traces without >10% loss in throughput
No increase in P95 latency > 15% for steady-state workloads
New metrics (margin_utilization, demotion_rate, kv_rehydrate_latency) emitted and dashboarded
On-call playbook for demotion-induced regressions documented and linked
Feature toggle and per-tenant margin override present
risks_and_tradeoffs: Demotion introduces rehydrate latency when evicted KV is needed shortly after — increases jitter for some requests
Keeping metadata about demoted entries increases host memory usage and complexity
Overly conservative margins reduce utilization and increase cost; under-conservative margins allow eviction storms
Interaction with quantization/weight offload: need safety checks to avoid simultaneous weight and KV offload creating disk/PCIe contention
observability_and_metrics: margin_utilization: fraction of margin currently consumed
kv_rehydrate_latency: latency distribution when demoted KV is reloaded
eviction_cascade_events: boolean/trace when cascading evictions detected
batcher_safety_trips: count of times batcher reduced window due to margin pressure
rollout_and_mitigation: Start on a non-critical region with small models + synthetic surge traces
Enable emergency kill-switch that disables demotion and restores prior watermarks
Gradual canary with traffic shadowing to measure rehydrate cost
If rehydrate latency > SLO, revert demotion style to host-only cache (no compression)
